description: The solution must ground on private enterprise data rather than model parametric knowledge alone.
Responses must be traceable back to the source they were grounded in.
The corpus is larger than fits in a single model context window.
The underlying source documents change frequently and must be kept fresh.
Different callers must see different subsets of the data based on their own entitlements.
The data involved includes personally identifiable information.
The data involved includes protected health information.
The solution must mutate a system of record, not just inform a human.
Action capability is explicitly planned for a later increment, not the current one.
At least one action the solution can take cannot be trivially undone.
Actions or decisions carry direct financial consequence.
The primary interaction mode is synchronous, multi-turn conversation.
The primary interaction mode is scheduled or event-triggered, with no user waiting synchronously.
Responses must return within a tight, human-perceptible latency budget.
Answering typical questions requires combining evidence from more than one retrieval hop.
Incoming queries are frequently ambiguous and benefit from query planning or clarification before retrieval.
The domain has a rich entity/relationship structure that answers must traverse.
The work required to satisfy a request is a variable, multi-step task rather than a single call.
The work decomposes into subtasks that are independent of one another and can run in parallel.
The work spans domains owned by different teams with different permission boundaries.
Expected request or record volume is high enough that per-unit cost and throughput matter.
Inputs include images, scans, or diagrams the model must read.
The primary data source is structured/tabular rather than document text.
A demonstrated, specific style/format/vocabulary requirement cannot be met by prompting or retrieval alone.
The requester has explicitly expressed a strong preference to reuse existing enterprise capability.
